title.value: Plasma phospho-tau217 for Alzheimer's disease diagnosis in primary and secondary care using a fully automated platform
title.quote: Plasma phospho-tau217 for Alzheimer’s disease diagnosis in primary and secondary care using a fully automated platform

design.value: Multi-cohort diagnostic accuracy validation of plasma p-tau217 using predefined biomarker cutoffs established in one secondary care cohort (Malmö) and then applied to four independent out-of-sample cohorts, four in secondary care and one in primary care
design.quote: we evaluated plasma phospho-tau217 (p-tau217) using predefined biomarker cutoffs. The study included 1,767 participants with cognitive symptoms from 4 independent secondary care cohorts in Malmö

n.quote: Overall, 1,767 patients with cognitive symptoms were enrolled ( n = 1,219 in secondary care; n = 548 in primary care).

n_description.value: patients with cognitive symptoms enrolled across the five cohorts (1,219 in secondary care, 548 in primary care)
n_description.quote: Overall, 1,767 patients with cognitive symptoms were enrolled ( n = 1,219 in secondary care; n = 548 in primary care).

population.value: 1,767 patients with cognitive symptoms (subjective cognitive decline, mild cognitive impairment or dementia) recruited while undergoing a memory investigation in clinical practice. CARE SETTING: 1,219 from four secondary care specialist memory clinics / outpatient neurodegenerative clinics — Memory Clinic of Skåne University Hospital (Malmö, Sweden, n=337), Memory Clinic of Sahlgrenska University Hospital (Gothenburg, Sweden, n=165), Cognitive and Behavioural Neurology Unit (Barcelona, Spain, n=487) and the outpatient neurodegenerative clinic of Brescia University Hospital (Italy, n=230); and 548 from a primary care cohort recruited from 19 primary care units in the south of Sweden, where patients sought medical help in primary care for cognitive symptoms. REFERENCE STANDARD: AD pathology defined by the CSF Aβ42:p-tau181 ratio measured with the FDA-approved Lumipulse assay (cutoff <11.94), or a positive [18F]flutemetamol PET visual read for the 87 primary care participants who could not undergo lumbar puncture.
population.quote: Overall, 1,767 patients with cognitive symptoms were enrolled ( n = 1,219 in secondary care; n = 548 in primary care).
population.location: Results, Participants and biomarker characteristics; Methods, Participants; Methods, Outcomes

comparator.value: Comparator index tests: the plasma p-tau217:Aβ42 (Lumipulse) ratio and a mass-spectrometry-based method for plasma %p-tau217 (p-tau217:np-tau217 × 100), both compared against Lumipulse plasma p-tau217 as secondary analyses
comparator.quote: As secondary analyses, we compared the performance of plasma p-tau217 with that of the p-tau217:Aβ42 (Lumipulse) ratio currently under FDA evaluation and a high-performing MS-based method for plasma %p-tau217

biomarker_confirmation.value: AD pathology determined by the CSF Aβ42:p-tau181 ratio on the FDA-approved Lumipulse assay with a cutoff of <11.94 derived by Gaussian mixture modelling; for 87 primary care participants unable to undergo lumbar puncture, a positive visual read of [18F]flutemetamol PET
biomarker_confirmation.quote: The primary outcome was the presence of AD pathology, which was determined by the CSF Aβ42:p-tau181 ratio analyzed using the FDA-approved Lumipulse assays

cohorts: BioFINDER-Primary Care study (primary care cohort, Sweden)

primary_endpoint_status.explanation: The document's primary outcome is the reference standard against which the plasma test was measured (AD pathology defined by CSF Aβ42:p-tau181) rather than a prespecified success threshold, so there is no primary endpoint that can be declared met or not met; the paper instead reports diagnostic accuracy figures and notes only an externally 'suggested requirement of ≥90% accuracy' that the single-cutoff approach did not reach in primary care (85%).
primary_endpoint_status.quote: The primary outcome was the presence of AD pathology, which was determined by the CSF Aβ42:p-tau181 ratio analyzed using the FDA-approved Lumipulse assays

multiplicity.approach: None — the document states results were not corrected for multiple comparisons; AUCs were compared using DeLong statistics and accuracies/PPVs/NPVs with a bootstrap hypothesis test
multiplicity.quote: Differences between AUCs were assessed using DeLong statistics. Results were not corrected for multiple comparisons.
multiplicity.location: Fig. 2 caption (and repeated in Figs. 1, 3–5 and Extended Data Fig. captions)

limitations: The present study has some limitations. First, our study included only European cohorts, necessitating further validation in clinical cohorts from other regions worldwide.
Second, the slightly lower performance compared with %p-tau217 in primary care settings and among older age groups highlights the need for further investigation.

Given the suggested requirement of ≥90% accuracy for BBMs in the diagnosis of AD , a two-cutoff approach for the Lumipulse p-tau217 assay might be necessary for its use as a stand-alone test for AD pathology, especially in primary care and across different age groups and cognitive stages
A two-cutoff approach might be necessary to optimize performance across diverse settings and subpopulations.
Accuracy was lower in participants aged ≥80 years (83%), but was unaffected by chronic kidney disease, diabetes, sex, APOE genotype or cognitive stage.
In primary care (Sweden), the accuracy was 85% (95% CI = 82–88%) (Fig. ), which was significantly lower than in secondary care (Supplementary Table ).
However, percentage p-tau217 had higher accuracy in primary care and was unaffected by age.
Using a two-cutoff approach, accuracies increased to 92–94% in secondary and primary care, excluding 12–17% with intermediate results.
In the two-cutoff approach, participants with an intermediate test result were not considered when calculating the accuracy, PPVs and NPVs, but have instead been specified in the figures.
This calculation assumes that 14.7% of patients fall into the intermediate group (the total proportion in the present study) and require further testing (Supplementary Table ).
However, in older individuals and those with CKD, the percentage of individuals with intermediate p-tau217 results increased to 19–20% (Fig. ).
Differences between AUCs were assessed using DeLong statistics. Results were not corrected for multiple comparisons.
Lumipulse plasma assays have not previously been validated with predefined cutoffs and have been examined only in single-center studies

risk_of_bias.judgement: The single and two-cutoff thresholds were both derived in the Malmö cohort, so the Malmö accuracy figures (89% single cutoff, 93% two cutoffs) are in-sample derivation results and are not independent validation.
risk_of_bias.quote: A single plasma cutoff was established in the Malmö cohort at 90% specificity (>0.27 pg ml −1 ), yielding an accuracy of 89% (95% confidence interval (CI), 86–93%) in the same cohort.

risk_of_bias.domain: spectrum / selection — age exclusion in one validation cohort
risk_of_bias.judgement: The Barcelona cohort, one of the four secondary care validation cohorts, excluded participants aged 80 years or older, the very group in which the assay's accuracy was found to be lowest.
risk_of_bias.quote: The exclusion criteria were: (1) age ≥80 years; (2) contraindication for lumbar puncture; or (3) disagreement with study procedures.

risk_of_bias.domain: reference standard incorporation / mixed reference standard
risk_of_bias.judgement: AD pathology was defined by CSF Aβ42:p-tau181 for most participants but by amyloid PET visual read for 87 primary care participants who could not undergo lumbar puncture; the reference standard therefore differs within the primary care cohort.
risk_of_bias.quote: For participants who could not undergo lumbar puncture in the BioFINDER-Primary Care study ( n = 87), AD pathology was determined based on a positive visual read of [ 18 F]flutemetamol PET.

risk_of_bias.domain: sponsor / manufacturer involvement in comparator measurement
risk_of_bias.judgement: The mass-spectrometry comparator assays were run by C2N Diagnostics, whose employees are coauthors, although the document states the analyses were blinded and C2N had no role in the statistical analysis.
risk_of_bias.quote: All C2N coauthors are salaried employees or consultants with cash and/or equity compensation from C2N Diagnostics. C2N Diagnostics performed the MS analyses blinded to any biomarker or clinical data and had no role in the statistical analysis or results.

risk_of_bias.judgement: Many pairwise comparisons across cohorts, subgroups, cognitive stages and assays were performed and the document states explicitly that no correction for multiple comparisons was applied.
risk_of_bias.quote: Differences between AUCs were assessed using DeLong statistics. Results were not corrected for multiple comparisons.

disagreements.question: Is a single predefined cutoff for the fully automated Lumipulse plasma p-tau217 assay sufficient for stand-alone diagnostic use?
disagreements.position: No — the document concludes that a two-cutoff approach, which leaves 12–17% of patients with intermediate results requiring further testing, might be necessary for stand-alone use, particularly in primary care, across age groups and across cognitive stages.
disagreements.quote: a two-cutoff approach for the Lumipulse p-tau217 assay might be necessary for its use as a stand-alone test for AD pathology, especially in primary care and across different age groups and cognitive stages

disagreements.question: Does chronic kidney disease compromise the accuracy of plasma p-tau217?
disagreements.position: This document reports that, contrary to prior work showing comorbidities affect blood-based biomarkers, accuracy of Lumipulse p-tau217 was not affected by CKD, although CKD did increase the proportion of intermediate results.
disagreements.attributed_to: Palmqvist and colleagues (this document), against prior reports that comorbidities impact BBMs
disagreements.quote: Comorbidities, especially CKD, are known to impact BBMs , . Notably, in our study the accuracy of Lumipulse p-tau217 was not affected by CKD.

disagreements.question: Does the plasma p-tau217:Aβ42 ratio improve diagnostic accuracy over p-tau217 alone?
disagreements.position: No — the ratio did not improve accuracy (and was significantly worse in primary care with two cutoffs), but it did reduce the proportion of intermediate results and raised NPV at the cost of PPV.
disagreements.quote: Using the plasma p-tau217:Aβ42 ratio did not improve accuracy but reduced intermediate test results (≤10%).

disagreements.question: Is the fully automated immunoassay equivalent to mass-spectrometry-based %p-tau217?
disagreements.position: Equivalent in secondary care, but inferior in primary care and in older participants, where MS-based %p-tau217 had higher accuracy and was unaffected by age.
disagreements.quote: Compared with a high-performing mass-spectrometry-based assay for percentage p-tau217, accuracies were comparable in secondary care. However, percentage p-tau217 had higher accuracy in primary care and was unaffected by age.
